# Summerlin West

Welcome to Summerlin West!

The Summerlin Master Planned Community is divided into four associations (Summerlin North, Summerlin South, Summerlin West and Summerlin Centre), which oversee two dozen commercial and residential villages. In this article I will go over what villages entails in Summerlin West and their locations.

## The Latest Listings in Summerlin West

## Summerlin West Overview

Summerlin West is a master-planned community located in the western part of the Las Vegas Valley in Nevada, within the city limits of Las Vegas. It is part of the larger Summerlin development, which is one of the most prominent and well-regarded planned communities in the United States.

Situated near the Red Rock Canyon National Conservation Area, Summerlin West offers residents scenic views of the surrounding mountains and desert landscape.
It is located west of the 215 Beltway and is known for its easy access to both outdoor activities and urban amenities.

Summerlin West is divided into 10 Villages, each with its unique character and housing options. The community offers a mix of single-family homes, townhomes, and luxury estates, catering to various preferences and lifestyles.

Summerlin West Villages include: The Vistas, The Paseos, Reverence, Stonebridge, Redpoint, Redpoint Square, Kestrel, Kestrel Commons, Grand Park, & La Madre Peaks. The zip code for Summerlin West is 89138.

## Real Estate Prices & Overview

Summerlin West median real estate price is $844,488, which is more expensive than 92.4% of the neighborhoods in Nevada and 86.4% of the neighborhoods in the U.S.

The average rental price in Summerlin West is currently $3,574, based on NeighborhoodScout's exclusive analysis. The average rental cost in this neighborhood is higher than 93.9% of the neighborhoods in Nevada.

Summerlin West is an urban neighborhood (based on population density) located in Las Vegas, Nevada.
Summerlin West real estate is primarily made up of medium sized (three or four bedroom) to large (four, five or more bedroom) single-family homes and townhomes. Most of the residential real estate is owner occupied. Many of the residences in the Summerlin West neighborhood are newer, built in 2000 or more recently. A number of residences were also built between 1940 and 1969.

Real estate vacancies in Summerlin West are 4.9%, which is lower than one will find in 65.0% of American neighborhoods. Demand for real estate in Summerlin West is above average for the U.S., and may signal some demand for either price increases or new construction of residential product for this neighborhood.

## Notable & Unique Neighborhood Characteristics

The way a neighborhood looks and feels when you walk or drive around it, from its setting, its buildings, and its flavor, can make all the difference.
This neighborhood has some really cool things about the way it looks and feels as revealed by NeighborhoodScout's exclusive research. This might include anything from the housing stock to the types of households living here to how people get around.

### People

In a nation where 1 out of every 4 children lives in poverty, the Summerlin West neighborhood stands out as being ranked among the lowest 0.0% of neighborhoods affected by this global issue.

In addition, according to NeighborhoodScout's exclusive analysis, Summerlin West is among the best neighborhoods for families in Nevada. In fact, this neighborhood is more family-friendly than 98.7% of neighborhoods in the entire state of Nevada. Its combination of top public schools, low crime rates, and owner-occupied single family homes gives this area the look and feel of a "Leave It to Beaver" episode. Many other families also live here, making it easy to socialize and develop a strong sense of community.

## Summerlin West FAQ

### What was the area west of Rainbow and south of Summerlin Parkway called?
That area is generally discussed as part of the west Las Vegas / Summerlin development corridor, with modern village naming tied to Summerlin West communities.

### How many villages are in Summerlin West?

Summerlin West includes multiple villages with distinct home styles, amenities, and HOA structures; inventory differs by village each week.

### What is the lifestyle like in Summerlin West Las Vegas?

Summerlin West blends newer luxury neighborhoods, elevated desert views, trail connectivity, and quick access to Red Rock Canyon, with Downtown Summerlin serving many retail and dining needs.

### Which newer Summerlin West villages are getting the most attention?

Buyers frequently compare Grand Park Village, Stonebridge, Red Point Square, and Kestrel Commons for newer layouts, modern finishes, and proximity to west-side amenities.

results.title: Best Neighborhoods in Summerlin Las Vegas 2026
excerpts:
* Amenities: You have access to over 10 golf courses, hundreds of parks, and top-tier healthcare facilities like Summerlin Hospital.
* Schools: The area boasts some of the highest-rated public schools in Clark County, along with prestigious private options like The Meadows School and Bishop Gorman.
* Cleanliness: The master association is very strict about maintenance. You won’t see broken down cars on lawns or unpainted walls.

The Cons:

* Price Premium: You pay for the name. The price per square foot in Summerlin is higher than almost anywhere else in the valley.
* Commute: While the beltway helps, if you work on the far east side or downtown Las Vegas, the commute can be 20 to 30 minutes.
* Strict Rules: Those strict maintenance standards I mentioned? They apply to you, too. You can’t paint your house a crazy color or park an RV in your driveway. The design guidelines are rigid.

## FAQs

### Which Summerlin village is the safest?
While Summerlin as a whole is known for being well-maintained and secure, the "safest" feel usually comes from the guard-gated communities. Villages like The Ridges and Red Rock Country Club offer 24-hour physical guard gates and roving patrols, providing the highest level of access control and privacy.

### Is Summerlin expensive compared to the rest of Las Vegas?

Generally, yes. Real estate in Summerlin commands a premium price per square foot compared to the general Las Vegas market. You are paying for the master-planned amenities, the trail systems, the proximity to Red Rock Canyon, and the higher-rated school zones.

### What is the difference between Summerlin North and South?

Think of Summerlin North as the "classic" area—it is quieter, has mature trees, and feels more established. Summerlin South is newer, buzzier, and closer to commercial hubs like Downtown Summerlin and the 215 Beltway.
South generally has more luxury custom home options, while North has more traditional suburban tract homes.

### Are there new homes available in Summerlin?

Yes, but they are concentrated in specific areas. If you are looking for new construction, you need to focus on Summerlin West. Villages like Stonebridge, Redpoint, and Kestrel are currently selling brand-new single-family homes, townhomes, and condos with modern amenities.

results.title: New Home Developments in Summerlin NV: 2026 Market Trends
excerpts:
The housing stock here is distinct from the resale market in older villages. We are seeing a massive shift toward "Desert Contemporary" architecture. Gone are the heavy stucco Mediterranean styles of the late 1990s. In their place, builders are delivering homes with clean lines, flat or shed rooflines, and a heavy emphasis on indoor-outdoor living to capture the desert scenery.

Buying new in 2026 offers distinct [advantages over the resale market](https://www.nevadarealestategroup.com/blog/investing-in-summerlin-real-estate/) . Beyond the modern aesthetic, these homes come with the latest energy-efficiency standards—crucial for managing desert summers—and builder warranties that you simply don't get with a 20-year-old house. While the master plan spans roughly 22,500 acres, the current energy is concentrated almost exclusively in Summerlin West.

## Summerlin West: The Epicenter of New Construction

If you are looking for new keys, you need to be looking West.
Specifically, west of the 215 Beltway. This area is divided into several "Districts" and "Villages," and navigating them can be a bit confusing if you aren't on the ground daily.

The development here is rapid, but it is organized. Right now, inventory is concentrated in a few specific villages, each offering a different lifestyle and price point.

### Grand Park Village

This is the next major focal point for the entire community. Grand Park Village is designed around a massive central gathering space—the Grand Park itself—which is slated to become a recreational hub rivaling the established parks in older Summerlin districts.

Builders here are just getting started or ramping up, offering a mix of housing types. The appeal of Grand Park Village is walkability and future access to green space. If you are buying here, you are buying into the promise of having one of the city's best amenity centers right outside your front door once completed this 2026.
### Kestrel & Kestrel Commons

Kestrel is currently one of the most active villages for sales. It sits slightly higher up the elevation gradient and offers a diverse mix of product types. You will find everything from detached single-family homes to luxury townhomes here.

Neighborhoods like Nighthawk and Vireo are good examples of what is available. Kestrel Commons is designed to be slightly more dense and connected, making it a strong option for buyers who want a lower-maintenance lifestyle without sacrificing the Summerlin address.

### Ascension (The Peaks)

If you are looking for luxury, Ascension is likely on your radar. This is a guard-gated enclave located in The Peaks district. It is positioned as a high-end destination, competing with resale homes in The Ridges but offering brand-new construction.

The pricing here reflects the exclusivity, often ranging from $1.5M to $3M.
